description: Somos parte de la escuela militar de aeronáutica, nuestra idea es crear un IA capaz de ayudar al astronauta en temas de salud espacial
summary:
MACCHI is an intelligent health-monitoring assistant designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. Our project combines artificial intelligence, health data management, and remote monitoring to create a more accessible and human-centered approach to astronaut healthcare.

We developed a functional prototype consisting of three interconnected components: MACCHI FACE, an interactive virtual assistant that communicates with astronauts; MACCHI CORE, which collects, stores, and analyzes health information; and MACCHI EARTH, which allows medical teams on Earth to remotely review health reports and trends.

MACCHI monitors indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, sleep quality, fatigue, and emotional well-being through health questionnaires and recorded measurements. It can identify changes over time and provide understandable information while keeping medical decisions under human supervision.

By addressing the challenges of isolation, communication delays, and limited medical assistance in space, MACCHI aims to improve astronaut autonomy and health awareness. The current prototype uses simulated data and demonstrates a foundation for future space healthcare technologies.
details:
MACCHI is an intelligent health-monitoring assistant designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It combines artificial intelligence, interactive communication, and health data management to make medical monitoring more accessible and human-centered.

The system consists of three interconnected components: MACCHI FACE, an animated virtual assistant that interacts with astronauts through voice and text; MACCHI CORE, which stores health records, analyzes indicators, and displays trends; and MACCHI EARTH, which enables remote health monitoring from Earth, including simulated communication interruptions.

MACCHI tracks indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep quality, physical activity, and emotional well-being. Its goal is to help astronauts understand their health, identify changes over time, and maintain communication with medical teams.

The project was developed using Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SQLite, and Google Gemini for conversational AI. It runs on conventional computers without requiring specialized hardware.

What makes MACCHI innovative is its combination of an expressive virtual companion with structured health monitoring and remote supervision. Our team prioritized accessibility, astronaut autonomy, data privacy, communication limitations, and user-friendly interaction.

Inspired by NASA and Canadian Space Agency research, MACCHI aims to contribute to future healthcare technologies for lunar and Martian missions. The current prototype uses simulated data and does not replace professional medical assessment.
